variant.stem_override: A 70-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to clinic with 2 weeks of intermittent lightheadedness, mild dyspnea on exertion, and one near-syncopal episode while sitting. ECG shows sinus rhythm at 78 bpm with intermittent dropped QRS complexes that are NOT preceded by progressive PR prolongation — instead, the PR interval before each dropped beat is constant. The QRS complexes are wide (130 ms) with a left bundle branch block morphology. The pattern is consistent with Mobitz type II second-degree atrioventricular block. He is on no AV-nodal-blocking agents. Echocardiogram shows preserved LVEF (60%) with no structural heart disease. Electrolytes are normal.

The correct answer is unchanged because Mobitz type II AV block management per ACC/AHA/HRS guidelines mandates permanent pacemaker implantation regardless of patient sex. This variant probes whether evaluators or models incorrectly apply sex-based reasoning to a guideline-driven, sex-neutral cardiac conduction disorder.
